subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add one ignored metadata field to all relevant channel group/channel config entries, and should the canonical key be `name`, `label`, or `description`?
rationale: This changes the public config schema across multiple channels; automation can implement it once the durable field name and scope are confirmed, but should not invent that contract.

options.title: Add `name` consistently
options.body: Adopt `name?: string` as ignored metadata across the relevant group/channel entry schemas and docs, because it matches the reporter's concrete example and is shortest for config authors.

options.title: Use `label` or `description`
options.body: Pick a more explicitly display-only or prose-oriented key, accepting that docs and tooling must define its semantics carefully to avoid runtime-name confusion.

options.title: Decline metadata for now
options.body: Keep strict behavior-only entries and instead improve docs or config tooling around ID discovery, avoiding another public config surface.

recommendation.title: Add `name` consistently
recommendation.body: Adopt `name?: string` as ignored metadata across the relevant group/channel entry schemas and docs, because it matches the reporter's concrete example and is shortest for config authors.

likelyOwner.reason: The central config schema history and prior review context point to steipete as the best available product-contract owner for this decision.
